children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--While the canola market is seen as "choppy" at the present time, an analyst  believes 2027 will be a good year for the Canadian oilseed.
"Long term, the demand side is excellent for canola," said Errol Anderson of Errol's Commodity Wire. "That's providing the crude-oil market doesn't suddenly plunge. If oil plunges, then down we go."
That said, what Anderson said he sees are tighter stocks in 2027 "that are going to keep prices elevated."
The analyst said the bottom end of the canola markets has been rising.

"If we have a selloff, $810 (per metric ton) is the bottom of the zone," he said, with resistance at C$840/ton. Should canola increase enough to push through that C$840, Anderson put the next level at C$880.

The path of crude oil has been the biggest driver guiding canola and other vegetable oils. With the U.S.-Iran war in the Middle East continuing to threaten oil supplies, crude prices are set to remain high.
Anderson said that over the last month canola jumped from C$770/ton to C$840.
Another factor is El Nino, specifically how the phenomenon will affect weather patterns, he said. "It's going to shift some production patterns."
Even with the Canadian canola harvest on the verge of swinging into high gear, Anderson doesn't believe pressure from it will last long.
"There's a firm tone to the whole market," he said.
